html:
Studio Misr is a film studio in Cairo founded in 1935 by the economist Talaat Harb. It made Egypt the centre of Arabic-language cinema for decades.

Talaat Harb had founded Banque Misr in 1920 to build Egyptian-owned industry against foreign capital. The studio was its most ambitious cultural project. It had modern sound stages, laboratories and equipment, sent young Egyptians to train in Europe, and brought in foreign technicians.

Its first film, Wedad (1936), starred the singer Umm Kulthum. The 1939 film The Will, by Kamal Selim, is often called the first great Egyptian realist film.

Through the 1940s and 1950s Egypt turned out dozens of films a year: musicals, melodramas and comedies watched from Morocco to Iraq. They spread the Egyptian dialect so widely that it became the most understood form of spoken Arabic. The studio was nationalised under Nasser in the 1960s. Compare the rise of the Hollywood film industry.
sum: Studio Misr is a film studio in Cairo founded in 1935 by the economist Talaat Harb. It made Egypt the centre of Arabic-language cinema for decades.
